body:
FILM ADR AMENDMENT — accept the additive route and typed denominator ruling, but LOCATOR versus DENOMINATOR is necessary and not sufficient. The current locator surface is not a mechanical rename. It contains several different operations whose laws are text-specific and must be classified separately in Stage A.

CURRENT-SOURCE EXHIBITS. core/span.scala defines TextSpan in UTF-16, orders SpanRef only by start/end/unit, and lets SpanSet.of sort/deduplicate, ++ merge, minSpan hull, coveredLength, and isContiguous on one implicit coordinate. core/claim.scala unions every span-bearing Evidence into one SpanSet. view/visibility.scala defines ReaderAt by endExclusive <= text offset and clips supports on that rule. view/compiler.scala and view/atlas.scala use minSpan/start/end for ordering, overlap, exact x geometry, and horizon-safe marks; view/codex.scala hashes those offsets into annotation identity and slices canonical text. features/space.scala turns minSpan.start into target position. align/source.scala is the single explicit denominator division. A heterogeneous film claim citing dialogue text, picture time, and audio cannot lawfully have one minSpan, one contiguity predicate, one reader horizon, or one renderer x without first choosing an axis.

The ADR inventory should therefore have an orthogonal OPERATION column, at least: (1) evidence membership/storage; (2) interval algebra/order/dedup; (3) content extraction; (4) epistemic-horizon clipping; (5) geometry/navigation/identity hashing; (6) denominator/normalization. Pure storage can move to heterogeneous EvidenceSupport. Every operation in 2-6 must select a typed stream/axis or refuse. This prevents the 48 wide sites from being described as one safe mechanical locator migration.

There is already a useful precedent and a trap in core/transcript.scala. AudioSpan is a typed half-open millisecond overlay, but TranscriptTurn retains SpanSet as master, and TranscriptAtlas explicitly requires audio order to agree with text order. That is correct for a transcript atlas and wrong as the film-source contract: film presentation time is primary; subtitle/dialogue text is an aligned stream; story-world order remains separate; an alternate cut or presentation-timebase needs its own immutable stream identity. Film must not inherit the text-master validation by reusing AudioSpan casually.

Recommended factorization for the ADR, without choosing wire names yet: heterogeneous nonempty EvidenceSupport owns typed anchors plus stream/source-bundle identity; an explicit projection operation yields an axis-specific extent only for one declared stream; cross-stream projection requires a checksummed alignment receipt; normalized position retains source kind, stream/edition identity, and measure semantics. Hull, overlap, adjacency, clipping, and ordering are defined only within one compatible axis. No generic mixed-support hull.

STORYATLAS COURT: every panel declares its projection axis; text, picture, and audio marks may be spatially synchronized only through a receipt; same normalized number on two axes creates no identity or selection edge; a mixed-evidence claim can show several tethers but no invented common x; missing stream alignment is a typed refusal. I recommend adding the operation classification and the existing TranscriptAtlas contrast to the approved Stage A ADR. This strengthens, rather than blocks, the chief ruling.
